# ARC prototype stamping

Use this pattern when an ARC grid has a repeated background, several isolated same-color marker cells, and one compact non-background prototype shape.

1. Identify the background color, isolated markers, prototype bounding box, and prototype motif.
2. Infer the prototype's anchor relative to each marker. In the observed task, the marker occupied the prototype's center cell.
3. Copy the prototype's non-background cells around every marker with the same relative offsets. Treat prototype-background cells as transparent; preserve the destination background rather than stamping the prototype background.
4. Replace each marker with the prototype's center/anchor value; retain the original prototype if the pattern indicates it remains in place.
5. Some tasks use the prototype itself as a motif to clone wherever that exact colored-cell silhouette fits entirely on an eligible destination color, rather than singleton markers as anchors. Infer the eligible destination color from the demo; do not assume it is the most common/background-looking color. In one demonstrated variant, the dominant field was 9, sparse cells were 0, and copies were stamped only where every prototype-colored offset landed on 0; the 9 cells were preserved. Search translations of the prototype's non-background offsets over the demonstrated eligible color, paint those cells with the prototype color, and keep the original. This applies to arbitrary motifs, not only straight lines: use every cell of the prototype color in its bounding box as offsets. Do not require the prototype's background-colored cells to match; they are transparent. Paint the union of all valid translations, including overlapping placements, while preserving every non-eligible destination cell. For a straight 3-cell line prototype, this means every eligible-color translated run of length three. The same rule applies to asymmetric motifs such as an L: derive the exact occupied offsets from the prototype and match all those offsets against the eligible color; do not require the motif's bounding-box gaps to match. For example, a 2x2 L prototype with occupied offsets at top-left, top-right, and bottom-left stamps at every translation where all three cells are eligible, painting their union while preserving all other cells. Be careful to use the demonstrated motif orientation and preserve all non-target cells.

7. Coordinate translation and motif orientation are easy to get wrong. Derive offsets directly from the colored prototype cells relative to its bounding-box top-left, then slide the shape through the grid at every in-bounds top-left. Validate the rule against the demo by comparing the union of predicted translated cells with exactly the cells that changed from background to motif color. This catches wrong offsets and wrong fill-color/background assumptions before applying it to a test.
6. Check all placements remain within grid bounds and don't overwrite unrelated structures, then submit the full output grid.

Observed example: a 3x3 motif was propagated centered on each singleton marker, with background-colored prototype cells transparent. Verify anchor and transparency from each new task's demo rather than assuming every prototype is centered.

## Connected line boundaries and edge cavities
Some puzzles show one or more connected orthogonal line arrangements rather than separate closed frames. Use demonstrations to identify rectangular cavities defined by horizontal/vertical line segments; a grid edge may function as the missing side of a cavity. Fill only the demonstrated interior cells with the demonstrated fill color, preserving all linework and unrelated regions. A single connected outline may contain multiple cavity-like regions, so infer bounds from the exact segments and validate against the demonstrated changed cells.

## Enclosed-region fill variant
A different pattern uses a single color (e.g. 3) to draw one or more outlines/frames, with a second color appearing in the demo output. If the demo shows the second color filling background-colored cells strictly enclosed by the outline while leaving the outline unchanged, fill all qualifying enclosed cells with that output color. Enclosures may be rectangular or irregular, and the linework may be connected or share boundaries; determine the actual enclosed cavities from connectivity rather than assuming rectangular frames. Use the demo to infer whether all enclosed background cells, only particular cavities, or a specific size/shape are selected, and infer the fill color. Preserve all outline and unrelated cells. Do not assume cavity sizes match.
